newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh stockmarket remains lifeless-- exchange.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh stockmarket remains lifeless-- exchange.

text.p: Kazakhstan's stockmarket -- potentially a major conduit for foreign investment into the resource-rich country -- remains lifeless due to poor infrastructure, stock exchange officials said on Wednesday.

"Six years (of reforms) have not led so far to the birth of Kazakhstan's stockmarket in the proper sense of the word," Kanat Meirmanov, president of the Central Asian Stock Exchange, told a news conference.

Investors interested in shares of large companies involved in extracting and processing Kazakhstan's huge natural resources, are "scared off by the lack of necessary stockmarket infrastructure", he said.

"We have not developed so far a system of independent registries, we have no depository. Also, there are no respectable insurance companies, as well as stable investment and pension funds," Meirmanov said.
"Thus, the system of transferring property rights has not been developed," said Erkin Bektayev, exchange council chairman.
21 large Kazakh companies are listed on the exchange, set up in December 1994, but there has so far been little demand for their shares, mostly due to their poor finances.
The exchange itself is loss-making, and trading volume amounted to only a tiny 115 million tenge in 1995-1996.

But Bektayev said that over the same period the exchange contributed over 907 million tenge to governemnt coffers by selling shares in state enterprises on government orders within the framework of Kazakhstan's cash privatisation.
And Bektayev said the exchange could eventually benefit from a typical emerging-market surge in share prices.
"Kazakhstan's stockmarket is a fledgling one, and this is what makes it attractive due to an eventual rapid growth of share prices," Bektayev said.
